prdTitle: PRD-11: Gradebook, Grading Scales & Report Cards
prdTicketRef: SCH-011 (PRD header). The pipeline ticket is SH-11.
brownfieldFindings: Assignment.categoryId, Quiz.categoryId, Course.gradingScaleId and every PRD-11 model (GradingScale, GradeCategory, GradeItem, Grade, TermGradeOverride, ReportCard) are missing from prisma/schema.prisma. They need a new migration.
GradeExemption (schema.prisma ~L801) already exists. Its comment says a row is the PRD-11 'exclude from gradebook' flag, so sync maps it to Grade.excused = true.
Submission has finalScore and returnedAt. A submission counts as returned when returnedAt is non-null.
Quiz.isPractice exists. Practice quizzes must never sync.

No function named getStudentQuizScore exists. The closest helpers are src/server/quiz/grading.ts (applyScoringPolicy, resultsVisible, percentOf) and quiz-service scoreOf. The architect should create or name getStudentQuizScore from these instead of duplicating them.
Section.homeroomTeacherId exists. Homeroom access already exists in src/server/auth/student-access.ts and attendance-service.
src/server/assignments/grading-math.ts has Decimal helpers, and src/server/csv.ts has CSV export. Reuse both.
src/config/student-tabs.ts has courses, attendance and assignments. Add grades and report-cards here.
No gradebook:backfill npm script exists yet. Seeding runs through 'db:seed' (tsx prisma/seed.ts).

functionalRequirements.description: Add enums GradeItemSource (ASSIGNMENT, QUIZ, MANUAL) and ReportCardStatus (DRAFT, PUBLISHED), plus the models GradingScale, GradeCategory, GradeItem, Grade, TermGradeOverride and ReportCard, exactly as specified, in a new prisma migrate migration.
Add Course.gradingScaleId (nullable, null = school default scale) and nullable categoryId to Assignment and Quiz. Add a category select to the assignment editor and the quiz editor.

When an assignment or non-practice quiz is published, upsert a GradeItem (source + sourceId, title, maxPoints, dueAt, category). Its term is the one containing dueAt (assignment) or availableUntil (quiz), falling back to the current term.
Unpublishing or archiving the source sets GradeItem.isVisible = false. Deleting the source deletes the GradeItem.
When a submission is returned, upsert its Grade with score = finalScore. Saving a grade without returning it must not sync.
A grade exemption (the existing GradeExemption row) sets Grade.excused = true. Removing the exemption clears it.
functionalRequirements.source: FR-2.2 'Exemptions set excused = true'; schema.prisma GradeExemption comment. The PRD does not state the clearing behaviour.

functionalRequirements.description: When a quiz attempt reaches GRADED and its results are visible, upsert Grade.score from the student's policy-applied quiz score (getStudentQuizScore), scaled to the quiz maxScore.

Add an idempotent one-time backfill script, `npm run gradebook:backfill`. It creates GradeItems and Grades for assignments, quizzes, submissions and attempts that existed before this PRD, and the seed runs it.
Grades written by sync are read-only in the gradebook UI and API except for comment. Grades on manual items are fully editable.

Add pure grade-calculation functions in src/server/gradebook/grade-calc.ts. They consider only visible items in the term whose grade is not excused. An item counts when it has a score, or when it is past due and marked missing (counts as 0). Ungraded items not marked missing are ignored.
Per category, drop the dropLowest lowest item percentages (never dropping every item). categoryPercent = Σscore / Σmax × 100.

Course percent is the weighted mean of category percentages, using only categories with at least one counted item and re-normalising weights to those categories. Uncategorised items form an implicit 'Uncategorised' category. A course with no categories uses total points earned / total possible × 100.

Round the percent half-up to 1 decimal place, then pick the first band of the effective scale (course scale, else school default) where percent >= minPercent. Example: 89.95 → 90.0 → A− in the seed scale.
TermGradeOverride percent and letter replace the computed values when set. A letter-only override keeps the computed percent.
The calculation must reproduce the worked example: Homework 40% (18/20, 9/10) and Exams 60% (70/100) gives 78.0% C+. The gradebook and the student Grades tab must both show it.

Add an admin page /admin/grading-scales with CRUD for grading scales and a band editor (letter, minimum %, optional GPA, descriptor). Validate that bands are strictly descending, the lowest minimum is 0, letters are unique, and exactly one scale is the default.

Add course Gradebook settings where the teacher manages categories (name, weight, drop lowest, order). A live sum indicator shows the weight total, and saving is refused unless weights total 100. Settings also include a course grading scale select that defaults to the school default.

Add a course 'Gradebook' tab for TEACHER/ADMIN with a term selector and an MUI X DataGrid (MIT). Columns are: students sorted by last name first, then items grouped by category via columnGroupingModel (header shows title, due date, max points, source icon), then category averages, then term percent + letter in bold. Use a sticky header (no pinned columns), horizontal scrolling and virtualisation for up to 60 students × 120 items.
Grid cells show the score, 'EX' (excused), 'M' (missing, red) or '—' (ungraded). Late submissions show a small clock icon.

Manual-item cells are editable through processRowUpdate. A user types a number, Enter or arrow keys move between cells, E marks excused, M marks missing and Delete clears. Changes save on blur with an optimistic update and per-cell error state.
Clicking a synced cell opens its source (the submission grading page or the quiz attempt).
Add an 'Add manual item' dialog with title, category, max points, date and term (POST /api/courses/:id/grade-items).
Add a student row action, 'Override term grade / comment', that opens a dialog with percent, letter and teacher comment (max 1,000 chars) and calls PUT /api/courses/:id/term-overrides/:studentId.
Item column menu actions: hide/show the item to students (isVisible), set all ungraded grades to missing (only after the due date), and view item statistics (average, median, high, low).
'Export CSV' exports the grid as displayed, reusing src/server/csv.ts or papaparse.

Register a student tab 'Grades' in src/config/student-tabs.ts. For the selected term it shows one card per course with percent, letter and colour (≥80 green, 60–79 amber, <60 red). Expanding a card shows each visible item (title, category, score/max, percent, comment, missing/excused flags) and category subtotals.
Add a /grades page for STUDENT and PARENT (parents get a child selector) that shows the same content as the Grades tab. Add a sidebar nav entry in src/config/navigation.ts.
functionalRequirements.source: FR-7.2; Platform Context 'A PRD that adds a page adds its nav entry'

functionalRequirements.description: Add a course tab 'Grades' for STUDENT/PARENT that shows that course's items only.

Add /admin/report-cards: select a term, then see a table of students (filter by grade level and section) with report card status (Not generated / Draft / Published) and missing-data warnings (for example ungraded items, or no teacher comment for a course).

'Generate drafts' (POST /api/report-cards/generate) builds a snapshot for each filtered student. It contains the school name/logo, student name, admission number, grade level, section, homeroom teacher, term and year. For each course it records subject, teacher, percent, letter, descriptor and teacher comment. It also records the term attendance summary (rate, absences, lates) and the grading scale legend.
Regenerating refreshes the snapshot of DRAFT cards only. PUBLISHED cards are never changed by regeneration or by later grade edits.
Add a per-card review page with a rendered preview. The homeroom comment is editable by the homeroom teacher or an admin, and the principal comment by an admin only (PATCH /api/report-cards/:id).
Add a /report-cards page where homeroom teachers list their section's drafts to write comments. Add a nav entry for TEACHER.

Publish (per card or in bulk for the filtered list) sets status PUBLISHED, publishedAt and publishedById, and sends report_card.published to the student and parents. Unpublish is admin only, requires a reason and writes an audit entry.

Add a print view /report-cards/[id]/print: A4 portrait, school letterhead, tables, signature lines for the principal and homeroom teacher, and @media print rules that hide the app sidebar. A 'Print / Save as PDF' button calls window.print(). Bulk 'Print all' renders the filtered published cards with page breaks.
Register a student tab 'Report cards' that lists published cards (students/parents) or all cards (admin/teacher). Each card opens the print view.
Report card access: ADMIN; the student's teachers; and the student and their parents only when the card is published. Any other student (for example in 7B) gets FORBIDDEN or NOT_FOUND.

Register notification types grade.posted (student + parents when a manual item grade is entered, default email false, one notification per student per item) and report_card.published (default email true) in src/server/notifications/types.ts, sent via notify().

Implement the REST endpoints in the API table with the listed roles. 'manage' and 'view' reuse the existing course-access checks, and GET /api/grading-scales is open to any authenticated user. Handlers are thin: Zod validators in src/lib/validators/gradebook.ts, then services in src/server/gradebook/, then the standard response and error shapes.
functionalRequirements.source: API table; Platform Context code layout

functionalRequirements.description: PUT /api/courses/:id/grade-categories replaces the full category list and validates that weights total 100.

Seed data: the default scale 'Standard A–F' (A 93, A− 90, B+ 87, B 83, B− 80, C+ 77, C 73, C− 70, D+ 67, D 63, D− 60, F 0, with descriptors); categories Homework 30 / Quizzes 30 / Exams 40 (drop lowest 1 homework) for all 7A courses; a manual item 'Oral presentation' in ENG-7A graded for all students; and draft Semester 1 report cards for 7A with teacher comments for MATH and ENG.
GET /api/students/:id/grades returns only visible items and only synced (returned or results-visible) scores, under the existing student-access rules (own student, linked parent, teacher, admin).

nonFunctionalRequirements.description: Correctness: grade calculation lives in pure functions, all arithmetic uses Decimal (Prisma.Decimal / the existing grading-math helpers), and an exhaustive unit test matrix covers no categories, empty categories, drop lowest, missing vs ungraded, overrides and rounding at band edges.
Performance: the gradebook for 35 students × 80 items loads in under 800 ms.
Performance: computing term grades for 600 students × 8 courses during report card generation finishes in under 30 s, using batched queries rather than per-student N+1 calls.
Auditability: every manual grade change, term override and report card unpublish writes an AuditLog row via audit(), with old and new values.
nonFunctionalRequirements.source: NFR-3; FR-8.4; Platform Context audit rule

nonFunctionalRequirements.description: Privacy: hidden items, unreturned assignment scores, not-yet-visible quiz results and unpublished report cards never appear in student or parent responses. This is enforced server-side.

Access control: every handler and server page enforces roles server-side (requireUser/requireRole plus per-entity checks). Teachers see only courses they teach and their homeroom section; parents see only linked students.

UI component rule: only Material UI (@mui/material, @mui/icons-material, @mui/x-data-grid, @mui/x-date-pickers, @mui/x-charts, @mui/x-scheduler) at the installed 9.5.0. Every component is looked up via the mui-mcp server (useMuiDocs and fetchDocs) before use, and only documented props are used. Banned libraries (Tailwind, shadcn, Radix, Recharts, @tanstack/react-table, notistack, etc.) and hand-styled raw HTML are not allowed. Toasts use useToast(), confirmations use Dialog and searchable selects use Autocomplete. QA verifies there are no banned imports.
DataGrid features are limited to the MIT tier: column groups and cell editing are allowed; pinned columns and other Pro/Premium-only features are not.

Brownfield: reuse existing models, services and helpers (course access, student-access, csv.ts, grading-math, quiz grading, notify, audit, logger, DataTable, useToast). Do not re-scaffold, rename routes or models, or add console.log. New code goes in src/server/gradebook/ and src/server/report-cards/.
Timestamps are stored in UTC and shown in SchoolSettings.timezone. 'Past due' and term-containment checks use the school timezone.
nonFunctionalRequirements.source: Platform Context Assumptions ('school timezone is the reference for every date rule')

nonFunctionalRequirements.description: Print view: each student's card fits on A4 portrait pages without the app chrome.

Quality gate: npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test pass. Add tests: unit (calculation matrix); integration (assignment-return and quiz-grading sync hooks, backfill idempotency, snapshot immutability); Playwright (teacher keyboard-edits manual grades, admin generates and publishes report cards, parent views a report card).
Scope: standards-based grading, GPA/class rank and multi-year transcripts are out of scope. GPA on a band is stored only and never computed.
nonFunctionalRequirements.source: Out of Scope; FR-1 bands gpa?

questions: FR-6: When a GradeExemption is removed, should the Grade revert to excused = false and re-sync the score?
FR-7: The PRD names getStudentQuizScore, but that function doesn't exist. Should the gradebook use the quiz's ScoringPolicy (best/latest/average) via applyScoringPolicy?
FR-13: The seed has a separate A− band at 90, so 89.95 → 90.0 maps to A−. Does the test requirement's label 'A' mean the A-band family?
FR-27/FR-33: Should /grades and /report-cards get sidebar nav entries?
NFR-10: Is 'past due' for missing items evaluated against dueAt in UTC or at end of day in the school timezone?
FR-3 term fallback: if dueAt falls outside every term and there is no current term, should the item be skipped or the sync error out?
unresolved: FR-6 exemption removal behaviour. Assumption: excused = false and the score re-syncs from source.
FR-7 quiz score source. Assumption: getStudentQuizScore is a new helper built on applyScoringPolicy + resultsVisible.
FR-13 89.95 → 90.0 maps to A− under the seed scale. Assumption: the test asserts 90.0 rounding and the letter of the 90 band (A−).
FR-27/FR-33 nav entries. Assumption: add them per the platform convention.
FR-3 no-term fallback. Assumption: skip creating the item and log a warning.
